## Overview

Submitting changes to Ulysses can be summarized as the following steps

1. Create a branch for your change
2. Create your changes
3. Submit your changes for review
4. Merge your changes

## Detailed workflow

### Create a branch for your change

To avoid working on an outdated codebase, ensure your local `main` branch is up to date and create
your feature branch off of the `main` branch.

Your feature branch must have the following name format

```
dev/<name>/<summary-of-change>
```

`<name>` can be your name or GitHub username.

`<summary-of-change>` is a short summary of the changes made on the feature branch.

Examples of good feature branch names are

```
dev/ubcrocketmember/add-imu-driver
dev/ubcrocketmember/fix-race-condition-in-baro-driver
```

Examples of bad feature branch names are

```
# A reader cannot determine what changes are being made
dev/ubcrocketmember/make-change

# Does not follow the branch name format
ubcrocketmember-fix-imu-driver

# Summary is too long. If you find yourself struggling to write a short summary
# of the changes, it is a sign that you should break it up into smaller feature branches.
dev/ubcrocketmember/add-this-and-that-feature-fix-x-and-y-and-refactoring-everything
```

### Create your changes

After making the necessary source code changes, you will have to create a commit for it.

Commit messages should follow the following format

```
<scope>: <summary-of-change>

<Optional commit message body>
```

`<scope>` is a short path indicating the scope of source code affected by your change. There is no
standard format for this, however, it should be short and informative. If you are unsure what to
put, check the commit history for that file to see what has been used before.

`<summary-of-change>` is a one-line summary of the changes being made in the commit.

Examples of a good commit message

```
docs: fix typo in development setup guide

The Cortex-Debug extension named was misspelled as Corex-Debug.
```

```
lib/matrix: fix overflow in matrix multiplication function

Fix overflow in matrix multiplication when large float values
were used by changing result type to double and promoting operands
to double. A double is guaranteed to fit the result of a float
multiplication.
```

Example of a bad commit message

```
Fix overflow in multiplication

Fix overflow in matrix multiplication when large float values
were used by changing result type to double and promoting operands
to double. A double is guaranteed to fit the result of a float
multiplication.
```

The above commit message does not properly follow the commit message format. A reader cannot easily
tell which part of the codebase was affected by this fix by reading the commit history.

### Submit your changes for review

After your changes are done, create a PR to the `main` branch of the repository.

Ensure the name of your PR follows the commit message format. In the body of the PR, provide
any information that could be useful to the reviewer (i.e. why you made the change, why the change
is written like this).

By default, the proper members will be requested to review the PR. However, you are free to add any
other members to review as well, although their reviews won't affect your ability to merge the PR.

> [!important] Keep your PR small
> For developers, you must keep your PR reviewable. A good guideline is that: If the change affects
> a large portion of the codebase, it must be kept simple (e.g. renaming a structure across the
> codebase). If the change is complex, it should be kept small.
>
> For reviewers, it is your responsibility to review the entire PR. For example, if it is a multi
> thousand line long PR with complex changes (e.g. add a new driver, changes the control algorithm
> and adds a new RTOS task), request that the PR author break it up into smaller reviewable PRs.

### Merge your changes

After your changes are approved, you are free to merge in the changes whenever.

However, ensure that you `squash and merge` the PR and that the squash commit's message is properly
updated. The squash commit message should be the name of your PR followed by the PR number (this
step is usually unecessary since GitHub should automatically generate the commit message name), and
you should update the commit message body to summarize why and what exact changes were made.

After merging, the branch should automatically be deleted from the repository. However, you may
still need to delete it locally.
